findings.fix: Restore the audience gate on the Welcome nav anchor: change `{{if initWelcome}}` back to `{{if and initWelcome isDeveloperAudience}}` (or add `{{if and initWelcome isDeveloperAudience}}` around it), so a casual-audience install started with --init-welcome never exposes the Welcome/setup/debug nav entry.
findings.claim: The diff deliberately dropped the isDeveloperAudience condition from the Welcome nav anchor, so any install run with --init-welcome shows the Welcome tab (and its setup/bootstrap/acdsl-internals content) to non-developer (casual) users, contradicting correctness-25's explicit requirement that the Welcome nav anchor be hidden for non-developer audience.
findings.evidence: git diff b4981b88d..e5245d08d -- internal/server/templates/layout.html shows the nav line changed from `{{if and initWelcome isDeveloperAudience}}Welcome{{end}}` to `{{if initWelcome}}Welcome{{end}}` — the audience check was removed. Re-read internal/server/templates/layout.html at the committed head (lines 25-45): line 28 now reads `{{if initWelcome}}Welcome{{end}}` with no isDeveloperAudience guard anywhere around it, while every other internals-exposing nav anchor (Config line 29, Skills/Context/Repos/Routines/Tools/Checklist lines 34-42) keeps its `{{if isDeveloperAudience}}` guard. Cross-checked server.go's initWelcome FuncMap (`"initWelcome": func() bool { return opts.InitWelcome }`) — it is a static server-construction flag independent of audience, and the code comment on welcomeTile in overview.go calls --init-welcome a debugging opt-in, so exposure is confined to installs explicitly started with that flag (rare, not default), keeping exposure at the lower-severity value per the cell rule even though the defect itself is unconditional whenever that flag is set.

findings.fix: Wrap the two action strings through translate: `action := translate(language, "click to filter this set")` / `action = translate(language, "click to clear the filter")` (stateNoteFor needs a language parameter threaded from groupViews, which already has `language` in scope), and add the two German strings to germanCatalog in i18n.go.
findings.claim: stateNoteFor builds every accepted/rejected/postponed state-note tooltip by concatenating an already-translated count phrase with a hardcoded English action suffix ("click to filter this set" / "click to clear the filter") that never passes through translate(), so on a German-language install these tooltips render as mixed German+English text, violating correctness-33's explicit requirement that vote-tooltip format strings be wrapped through the t/translate overlay.
findings.evidence: Re-read internal/server/proposals.go stateNoteFor (lines 581-605) in full: `action := "click to filter this set"` and `action = "click to clear the filter"` are plain Go string literals with no translate() call anywhere in the function, while the sibling `tooltip` argument passed in by groupViews (lines 450-454) is built via `fmt.Sprintf(translate(language, "%d of %d accepted"), ...)` — i.e. the surrounding code in the same file already follows the translate-wrap convention, making the two bare literals in stateNoteFor a clear omission rather than an intentional exception. Checked germanCatalog in internal/server/i18n.go for either string — absent. Confirmed this is reachable whenever a group's accepted/rejected/postponed count is nonzero or its filter is active (i.e., on most real Proposals-page views with data), but graded exposure at the lower value (rare) since it only manifests for installs that have opted into the German language profile, a non-default configuration.
